briefings.title: Academia Job Shortlist

scope.geography: United States; Cleveland/Ohio prioritized when a sufficiently strong match is available
focus: New Approach Methodologies and human-relevant technologies
Tissue engineering, biofabrication, microfabrication, and biomedical engineering
Translational gastrointestinal and inflammatory disease research
scope.selection_rule: Include only academic or academic-medical-center roles that materially advance the candidate's trajectory through scientific independence, a new platform capability, or direct ownership of human-relevant model systems; exclude generic postdocs and weakly related faculty searches.

candidate_profile_snapshot.headline: Biomedical engineering PhD candidate integrating experimental biology, computational fluid dynamics, and bioinformatics in human-relevant microphysiological systems.
core_strengths: Stretchable microfluidic gut-on-a-chip and multiplex organ-on-a-chip platforms
Patient-derived intestinal organoids and host-microbiome co-culture
Crohn's disease, inflammation, oxidative stress, radiation injury, fibrosis, and barrier dysfunction models
Single-cell and bulk RNA-seq, 16S analysis, pathway interpretation, and biological data integration
Computational fluid dynamics and transport modeling
Porous PDMS membrane fabrication, photolithography, soft lithography, additive manufacturing, and 3D printing
Translational NAMs and human-relevant alternatives to conventional animal testing
Wet-lab assay development, microscopy, barrier/function assays, molecular biology, advanced cell culture, troubleshooting, and experimental design

jobs.title: Associate Staff Scientist (Intestinal Organoids)
jobs.company_info: Cincinnati Children's is a major pediatric academic medical center. This opening is within the CuSTOM Accelerator, a multidisciplinary translational program connecting organoid biology with clinicians, surgeons, bioengineers, computational scientists, automation, imaging, drug discovery, predictive toxicology and regenerative medicine.

salary.note: Range surfaced in the current job listing; verify the institutional range during application because academic salary displays can vary by source.

jobs.job_description: Lead optimization and characterization of human intestinal organoid platforms, including iPSC-derived systems, and translate them toward disease modeling, drug discovery, predictive toxicology, precision medicine and regenerative applications. Work independently while collaborating with bioengineering, automation, imaging and data-science teams.
key_must_have_requirements: PhD in biology, bioengineering, developmental/stem-cell biology, tissue engineering, regenerative medicine or a closely related field
Strong human iPSC, adult stem-cell or intestinal organoid experience
Extensive mammalian cell culture and independent experimental ownership
Quantitative characterization using imaging, molecular assays and transcriptomic/single-cell approaches
Ability to work across multidisciplinary translational teams
preferred_requirements: Python, R, MATLAB, C++ or LabVIEW
jobs.why_good_match: This is almost a direct academic mirror of the current research identity: intestinal organoids, organ-on-chip/MPS, patient-relevant models, single-cell analysis and translational applications are all central rather than peripheral. The candidate also brings microfluidics and model-engineering depth that a conventional organoid biologist may not have.
specific_experience_to_highlight: Patient-derived intestinal organoid culture and differentiation
Crohn's disease organoid and gut-on-chip models
gaps_or_risks: Direct iPSC-derived intestinal organoid experience may be less extensive than adult patient-derived organoid experience
Flow-cytometry and automation experience may be lighter than some preferred candidates
Staff-scientist roles can be excellent technically but may offer less protected independence than a strategically chosen postdoc
resume_tailoring: Lead the CV with intestinal organoids and human-relevant GI models
Make organ-on-chip/MPS a major differentiator because it is explicitly preferred
Put scRNA-seq and computational interpretation alongside wet-lab organoid expertise
In the cover letter ask how much project ownership, grant participation and first/senior-author publication opportunity the role provides
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply now and contact the CuSTOM team directly. Before accepting any interview path, clarify scientific ownership, publication expectations and advancement because the technical fit is outstanding but the long-term value depends on independence.

jobs.title: Post Doctoral Scientist - Cardiovascular Development
jobs.company_info: Nationwide Children's is a major pediatric research institute in Columbus. The Zhao laboratory combines patient-derived iPSCs, CRISPR/Cas9, organoids and single-cell genomics to study cardiovascular development and congenital heart disease.

salary.note: Current listing range; verify final postdoctoral scale and experience-based placement with the institution.

jobs.job_description: Use patient-derived iPSCs, genome editing, organoid models and single-cell genomics to study cardiovascular development and congenital heart disease, with translational applications and opportunities to integrate bioinformatics and tissue engineering.
key_must_have_requirements: PhD, MD or equivalent doctoral training appropriate for the postdoctoral appointment
Strong experimental research record
Relevant expertise in cardiovascular development, genomics, organoid biology or related systems
Ability to conduct independent research under mentorship and publish rigorously
jobs.why_good_match: The postdoc preserves the strongest existing assets—organoids, engineered models and single-cell analysis—while adding three capabilities that would genuinely broaden a future PI profile: iPSC biology, CRISPR and a second organ system. That is more valuable than another gut-chip postdoc that simply repeats the PhD.
gaps_or_risks: Cardiovascular development is outside the current GI focus
Direct iPSC and CRISPR experience may be limited
A postdoc is worthwhile only if it provides independent project ownership and a strong publication/funding trajectory
resume_tailoring: Frame the transition as adding iPSC/genome-editing capability to an established organoid/MPS foundation
Do not overemphasize gut-specific disease details
Highlight ability to learn new organ systems while retaining a coherent human-model engineering identity
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply and email the PI with a short research-fit note. Ask specifically what project could be independently owned and whether the postdoc can develop an F32/K99-style funding trajectory.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Scholar Research - Cardiovascular 3D Printing & Bio-Innovation Laboratory
jobs.company: University of South Florida Health Heart Institute
jobs.company_info: USF Health's newly established Ruberg Cardiovascular 3D Printing & Bio-Innovation Laboratory integrates 3D printing/bioprinting, tissue engineering, stem-cell and cell biology to develop next-generation cardiovascular research platforms.

salary.note: Range surfaced in the current listing; confirm final institutional postdoctoral salary.

jobs.job_description: Advance research in a new cardiovascular bio-innovation lab combining cellular/stem-cell biology, 3D printing and bioprinting, and tissue engineering. Responsibilities include experimental design, cell-based research, quantitative analysis and scientific dissemination.
key_must_have_requirements: Doctoral training relevant to biomedical engineering, tissue engineering, cell biology or a related field
Strong hands-on experimental research capability
Ability to independently design experiments and analyze data
Strong scientific writing and communication
jobs.why_good_match: This is the strongest academic option for turning additive manufacturing into a serious biomedical research specialization. The candidate already knows 3D printing, microfabrication, engineered tissues and wet lab biology; a bioprinting-focused postdoc would add a new platform rather than duplicate the gut-chip PhD.
specific_experience_to_highlight: Cell culture and engineered tissue models
gaps_or_risks: Direct bioprinting and bioink formulation may be limited
Cardiovascular biology is a new disease area
A new laboratory can offer unusual ownership but may also have less established infrastructure and publication history
resume_tailoring: Show fabrication images and technically difficult devices
Explain how current organ-chip fabrication experience transfers to bioprinting and tissue construction
Ask how much freedom exists to create an independent research direction
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply with a one-page fabrication portfolio. During the first conversation, test whether the lab will let you own a biofabrication platform rather than serve mainly as the person who operates the printer.

jobs.title: Research Scientist I - Organoid Core
jobs.company_info: Tulane's Patient Derived Organoid Shared Resource supports the Tulane Cancer Center and Louisiana Cancer Research Center. The role is the primary technical specialist/operator for a patient-derived organoid core serving translational research programs.
jobs.job_description: Serve as the primary technical specialist for a patient-derived organoid shared resource, supporting organoid culture, platform operation, research projects and investigators using organoid models within a cancer-center environment.
key_must_have_requirements: Advanced research training appropriate for a research-scientist role
Strong organoid and mammalian cell-culture skills
Independent technical troubleshooting and reproducible platform operation
Ability to support multiple investigators and document shared-resource workflows
jobs.why_good_match: Patient-derived organoids and reproducible model operation are already core strengths, so the technical ramp would be short. The role could also provide broad exposure to many disease programs and collaborators rather than one PI's project portfolio.
specific_experience_to_highlight: Model quality control and quantitative phenotyping
Translation of organoids into microphysiological platforms
gaps_or_risks: Cancer biology is not the current primary disease area
Core roles can become service-heavy and reduce first-author scientific ownership
Long-term PI preparation depends heavily on whether independent projects and grants are allowed
resume_tailoring: Emphasize reproducibility, protocol development, troubleshooting and training others
Frame organ-on-chip as an extension capability for the core
Ask directly about independent publications, grant participation and ability to develop new core technologies
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply if a research-scientist path is attractive, but treat project ownership as a gating question. A well-paid organoid service role is not automatically a better career move than a lower-paid postdoc with strong independence.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow - Spatial and Single-Cell Multi-Omics
jobs.company: Mount Sinai Health System / Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
jobs.company_info: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is a major biomedical research institution. This postdoctoral opening focuses on developing, optimizing and applying spatial and single-cell multi-omic methods within a collaborative research environment.
jobs.location: United States / Mount Sinai research program

salary.note: Salary was not surfaced in the current listing used for this shortlist.

jobs.job_description: Develop, optimize and apply spatial and single-cell multi-omic approaches, integrating high-dimensional molecular measurements with biological questions and collaborative projects.
key_must_have_requirements: Doctoral training relevant to genomics, computational biology, molecular biology or a related discipline
Strong research and data-analysis foundation
Ability to learn or develop single-cell/spatial methods
Collaborative scientific communication
preferred_requirements: Integration of molecular data with experimental biology
jobs.why_good_match: The candidate already has single-cell analysis tied to engineered human models. A spatial/multi-omic postdoc could turn bioinformatics from a supporting skill into a genuine second pillar and create a stronger future niche around spatially resolved biology in organs-on-chip.
specific_experience_to_highlight: Linking cell states to functional experimental phenotypes
gaps_or_risks: The position may use little device engineering or tissue fabrication
A computational-methods postdoc could pull the career away from organ-chip platform development if not intentionally connected back to human model systems
resume_tailoring: Lead with single-cell data and biological interpretation
Present wet-lab experience as an advantage for designing interpretable omics experiments
In the research statement propose spatial/single-cell analysis of engineered human tissue systems as the bridge between old and new expertise
jobs.immediate_action_now: Investigate the lab's disease/model focus before applying. Prioritize it only if the postdoc can connect spatial multi-omics back to organoids, engineered tissues or other human-relevant systems rather than becoming a generic computational postdoc.

briefings.overall_takeaway: Academia is stronger in Ohio this week than industry. Cincinnati Children's is the clearest direct fit because it explicitly combines intestinal organoids, MPS/organ-on-chip, predictive toxicology, single-cell methods and translational model development. For a postdoc, Nationwide and USF are strategically stronger than simply repeating the current gut-chip work because they add a genuinely new capability—iPSC/CRISPR or bioprinting—while preserving the human-model engineering identity.
